stem:
Karan forms values with the four fixed numbers $7$, $4$, $2$, and $1$ by writing $7\pm 4\pm 2\pm 1$ and choosing each sign independently.

Which claim correctly decides whether changing the signs can change the odd/even parity of the value?

options.text: Yes: each sign change flips the parity of the value.
No: every choice of signs gives a value with the same parity.
Only the sign in front of $7$ can change the parity.
Yes when the four numbers are consecutive, and no for these four numbers.

teacher.key_rationale: Changing a sign replaces +t with -t (or the reverse), which changes the total by 2t, an even amount, so parity is fixed for all sign choices. Claiming every flip changes parity omits that even shift. Singling out 7 or restricting to consecutive numbers mis-scopes the rule.
